title: Join slices compare with coherent cocone categories, including fixed apex fibers
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent cocones, functor equivalences and Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For small simplicial sets $X,Y$ define $(X\star Y)_n=X_n\amalg Y_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}X_a\times Y_b$, with operators restricting the ordered $X$-block followed by the $Y$-block. Let $a:L\to\mathcal E$ be any small simplicial diagram in a quasicategory. Define the join slice $J_a$ to have $n$-simplices the maps $L\star\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $a$ on $L$, with operators induced by $\operatorname{id}_L\star\Delta(\alpha)$, and projection $J_a\to\mathcal E$ given by restriction to $\Delta^n$. Let $P_a=\{a\}\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E),\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E))\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)}\mathcal E$ be the coherent cocone category, with its apex projection. Define the fat join $L\diamond X=L\amalg_{L\times\{0\}\times X}(L\times\Delta^1\times X)\amalg_{L\times\{1\}\times X}X$. Restricting the initial and final blocks gives a natural map $L\diamond X\to L\star X$, identical on $L$ and $X$. Precomposition for $X=\Delta^n$ defines a comparison $J_a\to P_a$. This comparison is a functor equivalence of quasicategories over $\mathcal E$. For every vertex $T$ of $\mathcal E$, both strict fibers over $T$ are Kan complexes and the comparison induces an equivalence $J_a\times_{\mathcal E}\{T\}\to P_a\times_{\mathcal E}\{T\}$. The latter target is the space $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)}(a,\Delta_LT)$ of coherent cocones, up to its natural mapping-space equivalence. These comparisons are natural in $a,L,\mathcal E$, including restriction of the indexing shape, and in the apex, with postcomposition interpreted through coherent composition. A vertex of $J_a$ is initial if and only if its associated coherent cocone is colimiting. The assertions include $L=\varnothing$.

Corollary 4.2.1.8 applied in Fun(L,E) compares the unpinched fixed-endpoint fiber to the specified right-pinched mapping space. The fat-join adjunction identifies the fat slice with the coherent cocone category. No Stacks tag for this comparison.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)$. The exponential-corner theorem makes $D$ a quasicategory (use $\varnothing\hookrightarrow L$ and $\mathcal E\to *$). Restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\to D\times D$ is an isofibration, using $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. Pull it back along $\mathcal E\to D\times D$, $T\mapsto(a,\Delta_LT)$. Its pullback is exactly $P_a$, and the pullback projection $P_a\to\mathcal E$ is an isofibration: any inner-horn or source-specified equivalence-edge lifting problem projects to one for the original isofibration, and its lift together with the prescribed base map is a lift into the degreewise pullback. For an inner horn in $P_a$, first fill its projection in $\mathcal E$, then lift that filler, so $P_a$ is a quasicategory. By the sharp-cocone theorem $J_a=S_a(\mathcal E)$ is a quasicategory and its apex projection is an isofibration. No restriction on $L$, including nonemptiness, has entered.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.5, preparatory fibrancy and endpoint restrictions; read online, archive WANTED; agent expansion using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: For every small simplicial set $R$, put $A_R=\operatorname{Fun}(L\star R,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)}\{a\}$ and $B_R=\operatorname{Fun}(L\diamond R,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)}\{a\}$. The restriction maps to $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)$ are isofibrations, since both pure inclusions of $L$ are degreewise injective. The blunt-to-sharp comparison gives a functor equivalence of the unrestricted functor objects, strictly over this base, since it fixes $L$. Isofibration base change along the vertex $a$ gives an equivalence $r_R:A_R\to B_R$ between quasicategories. There is a simplicial isomorphism $B_R\cong\operatorname{Fun}(R,P_a)$: in parameter degree $m$, a map $(L\diamond R)\times\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$ with prescribed $L\times\Delta^m$ is, by the defining quotient, an apex map $R\times\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$ and a cylinder map $L\times\Delta^1\times R\times\Delta^m\to\mathcal E$, equal at $0$ to $a\operatorname{pr}_L$ and at $1$ to the constant-in-$L$ apex. Products preserve this quotient because its generating relations retain the parameter coordinate. Currying is precisely the displayed cocone pullback. Also maps $e:R\to J_a$ correspond bijectively to vertices $F_e:L\star R\to\mathcal E$ of $A_R$ by the sharp-join universal property. Under these identifications $r_R(F_e)$ is exactly $ce:R\to P_a$, where $c$ is the comparison in the item. This is only an object bijection on the sharp side; no isomorphism $\operatorname{Fun}(R,J_a)=A_R$ is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.5, sharp/fat adjunction and restriction to the fixed diagram; read online, archive WANTED; agent expansion using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: We check precisely how the object bijection $e\mapsto F_e$ treats equivalences. Let $I=N(\{0\cong1\})$ be the invertible interval of the cited interval theorem. For any small $R$, projection $R\times I\to R$ is a categorical equivalence. Indeed it has the section at $0$; the unique arrows $0\to i$ in the two-object groupoid give a natural isomorphism from its constant-$0$ endofunctor to its identity, hence a simplicial homotopy on $R\times I$. For every quasicategory $Q$, precomposition gives quasi-inverse functors on the functor objects: the remaining composite is naturally equivalent to the identity, because at each vertex its component is the image of an invertible groupoid arrow. The pointwise-equivalence theorem verifies that this is an equivalence edge, and the Joyal functor-equivalence test identifies the projection as a categorical equivalence. Therefore $\overline B=L\star(R\times I)\to B=L\star R$ is a categorical equivalence by preservation under joins. The two endpoint sections agree on $L$, have composite identity with this projection, and induce a degreewise injection $B\amalg_L B\hookrightarrow\overline B$: the two pure $R$ copies and mixed $L$-$R$ blocks are disjoint unless in the common pure $L$ summand. Thus this is a categorical mapping cylinder for $B$ relative to $L$. The relative categorical cylinder criterion says that $F_{e_0}$ and $F_{e_1}$ are equivalent vertices in $A_R$ exactly when there is a map $L\star(R\times I)\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $a$ on $L$ and to those two maps at the endpoints. By the sharp-join universal property this is the same as a map $R\times I\to J_a$ with endpoints $e_0,e_1$. Currying and the invertible-interval theorem in the quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(R,J_a)$ say this is equivalent to a coherent natural equivalence between $e_0,e_1$. Here functor objects are quasicategories by the exponential-corner theorem. For completeness, isomorphism in $hQ$ is the same as existence of an equivalence edge: the triangle-calculus theorem represents an isomorphism and its inverse by edges and realizes both inverse equations by the two triangles required by the definition. All maps in this argument fix the prescribed boundary $a$ throughout the homotopy.

proof.text: For every small $R$, step 3 makes $e\mapsto F_e$ a bijection on classes of vertices modulo coherent natural equivalence. Step 2's functor equivalence $r_R$ also induces a bijection on such classes, using its quasi-inverse and its two natural-equivalence witnesses. Their composite, by its explicit identification in step 2, is postcomposition with $c:J_a\to P_a$. Use surjectivity at $R=P_a$ to get $g:P_a\to J_a$ with $cg\simeq1_{P_a}$. Whiskering by $c$ gives $c(gc)\simeq c(1_{J_a})$. Injectivity at $R=J_a$ gives $gc\simeq1_{J_a}$. These are exactly a quasi-inverse and the two coherent natural equivalences, so $c$ is a functor equivalence. Enlarge the universe once to contain these test shapes when needed; all constructions above hold in that universe. It is over $\mathcal E$ strictly: restriction to the final block agrees with the apex map in the fat-join quotient in every simplicial degree.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.5, explicit quasi-inverse recognition; read online, archive WANTED; agent expansion using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Both apex maps in step 1 are isofibrations, and $c$ is an equivalence strictly over the common quasicategory $\mathcal E$. Apply isofibration base change with $R=\Delta^0$ and the map selecting any vertex $T$. It gives an equivalence of the strict fibers. The coherent fiber is exactly $U_D(a,\Delta_LT)$: its $n$-simplices are arrows parametrized by $\Delta^n$ with both endpoints constant, directly from the displayed definition of $P_a$. The pinch-comparison theorem says this is Kan and gives the natural equivalence from the specified right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_D(a,\Delta_LT)$ to this fiber. To check Kan structure on the sharp fiber independently, reverse simplices. The explicit join formula identifies $(J_a)^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the sharp slice $(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}})_{/a^{\mathrm{op}}}$ on $L^{\mathrm{op}}$. The opposite theorem ensures $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. The general sharp-slice theorem makes this projection a right fibration, and the right-fibration fiber theorem makes its strict fibers Kan. The opposite of a Kan complex is Kan, since reversal sends each horn $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$ and carries a filler back to a filler. This proves that the original sharp fiber is Kan. Thus the comparison of strict fibers is an equivalence of Kan spaces, not merely an equivalence of their homotopy categories.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.6; Corollaries 4.2.1.7-4.2.1.8; dual of Proposition 2.1.2.1; read online, archive WANTED; agent expansion using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: For $u:L'\to L$ the sharp side restricts by $u\star\operatorname{id}$ and the fat side by $u\diamond\operatorname{id}$. For $v:R'\to R$ the same is true in the final block. The collapse commutes with these maps: on a cylinder simplex with interval coordinate $t:[n]\to[1]$, both composites take the $L$ coordinate on $t^{-1}(0)$ and the final coordinate on $t^{-1}(1)$. Postcomposition by any $\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ also commutes with these formulas and all endpoint restrictions. Hence the comparisons are natural in shape, diagram, and target. On fixed-apex fibers these formulas agree with the natural pinch comparison, since both pinch maps split the same interval into its two blocks. For an apex arrow $h:T\to T'$, the coherent fiber is $U_D(a,\Delta_LT)$ and its transport sends a cocone $\lambda$ to the coherent composite $\Delta_L(h)\lambda$; this retains the composition homotopies. The cocone projection itself supplies these transport diagrams, and $c$ is a map over $\mathcal E$, hence takes a diagram over $h$ to the corresponding diagram over $h$. To make the transport interpretation precise, the sharp apex projection is a left fibration by reversing the right-fibration assertion in step 5. On the coherent side the fixed-source arrow projection in $D$ is a left fibration, by applying the fixed-target-arrow right-fibration theorem to $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reversing simplices; $P_a$ is its pullback along $\Delta_L$. The mapping-space opposite comparison in the opposite theorem identifies the reversed fibers. Thus these diagrams encode the usual coherent composition, including all higher apex compatibilities; no strictly chosen composition functor is required.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.5 and Corollary 4.2.1.7, naturality of the join collapse and its fixed-fiber comparison; read online, archive WANTED; agent expansion using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: The definition of a colimiting coherent cocone is initiality in $P_a$. A functor equivalence induces equivalences on every mapping space by the enhanced functor/cone calculus, so the equivalence $c$ preserves and reflects initial objects. Explicitly, for an initial $j\in J_a$ and any $p\in P_a$, choose $j'$ with $cj'\simeq p$ by step 4; then $\operatorname{Map}_{P_a}(cj,p)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{J_a}(j,j')$ is contractible. Here replacing $p$ by the equivalent object $cj′$ induces a mapping-space equivalence: compose with the chosen equivalence and its inverse; the associative and unit homotopies of the mapping-composition theorem show that these two induced maps are homotopy inverses. The reverse implication tests objects $cj'$ and uses the same mapping equivalence. A vertex $j$ is the right-join cocone $L\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal E$, and its image under $c$ is exactly its induced coherent transformation by step 2. This proves the initial/colimiting characterization. For $L=\varnothing$, both $L\star R$ and $L\diamond R$ are $R$, $D=\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,\mathcal E)$ is terminal, and $J_a=P_a=\mathcal E$ with comparison the identity; both fixed-apex fibers are a point. For nonempty $L$ with $\mathcal E=\varnothing$ there is no input $a$; for $L=\varnothing=\mathcal E$ the total categories are empty and the assertions about vertices and fibers are vacuous.
